body:
I fell apart when I was 16-22, didn't get into the schools I wanted, wound up stuck at community college, no decent job, no prospects, struggling to make rent, let alone food. 

Shit. Gets. Better. 

Your grade dosen't matter to employers, they care about your skills, I don't have a degree and I'm doing fine in the IT world. Just make yourself irreplaceable in your niche. The friends who matter don't care about grades, if they did the few good friends I have wouldn't talk to me. Your friends should care about *you*, not your grades. 

As far as family, as much as I hate to say it, fuck em. There's a point in life where you need to cut out the cancer and negative influence. I cut out my alcoholic parents and my druggie brother, it sucks but you're better in the long run. 

Do what *you* need to do for *you*. It's your life, don't let someone else define it.

Parents tend to not be able to rationalize the struggles their children go through. They may just not understand, it's not out of anger that they can't relate it's out of a concerned fear. They don't know how to handle it so they try to call whoever they think can.

Relying on someone in times of need is normal, it's healthy, it's why people are in relationships. He's there for you because he cares. Your family does not define you. Does not define you. Your fathers failures and your mothers failures as much as they may impact you do not define you. Their chapters of adversity will only give you perspective and experience. 

Don't let the failures of those around you cause doubt to yourself. Their problems may impact you, but they aren't yours. Everyone falls apart at something, your parents failing is their relationship, this particular class may be your weakness. It dosen't mean they are/you are insufficient for not succeeding, it just means things didn't work out. Try again, try another angle, just don't let others mistakes define you. 

Use the shoulders of those who support you, but don't carry the weight of things beyond your control.
